title: Edge throttle playtest scribbles — APAC midday run
content:
Context:
Quick scribbles from the APAC edge throttle playtest executed 2026-10-29 (midday window). Primary goal: validate throttle + fallback behavior when regional priming is insufficient and to capture human-in-the-loop handoff signals for ops. This is a working record — not a formal runbook yet.

High-level summary:
- Test window: 2026-10-29 11:30–13:00 SGT (approx).
- Regions targeted: ap-southeast1 (Singapore edge pods), ap-northeast1 (Tokyo as secondary).
- Workload shape: synthetic steady baseline + three burst waves (3x, 6x, 10x multiplier) with mixed short-chat and long-context gen (avg request length 45 tokens, long tail to 2k).
- Key intent: exercise throttle token exhaustion, prefix cache misses, and automatic regional fallback policy.

Observations / telemetry highlights:
- Baseline (pre-burst): 95th p50/p95 latencies ~ 48 / 78 ms for short gen on local edge pods; token cost baseline in line with expected.
- Wave 1 (3x): smoothly absorbed by local autoscale (cold pool warmed from primed reserves). Minor KV-cache churn; p95 ~ 112 ms. No fallbacks.
- Wave 2 (6x): observed throttle token queue growth (queue depth to ~320 requests) at ~+14m into the burst; local tail-latency p99 spikes to 420 ms for long-context. Autoscale backed by regional burst capacity but with ramp delay. Two requests dropped by the edge balancer due to token exhaustion -> triggered immediate fallback to Tokyo. Fallbacks completed with avg extra latency +280 ms.
- Wave 3 (10x): Sustained token pressure; local pool hit configured max-concurrency. Fallback rate increased (approx 38% of requests routed to tokyo fallback policy). Token reuse/caching efficiency fell by ~21% due to new prefixes in synthetic workload. Observed transient error class: 503s with balancer message "throttle-token-exhausted" (approx 0.6% of requests during peak).

What surprised us:
- Prefetch/priming latency: When priming was started on adjacent nodes at time-of-burst, cache fill rate lagged expected values by ~40s due to colder-than-expected KV distribution; suggests our priming heuristics under-count new-prefix variety in these synthetic mixes.
- Tokyo fallback path introduced unexpected cold-start tail for a small fraction of sessions because destination model variant use differed (quantized vs fp16) -> minor generation artifacts noticed by QA.
- Some autoscale signals (pod_ready_count) oscillated under CPU pressure because the sidecar metrics emitter aggregated at 15s windows — we lost finer-grained reaction ability.

Action items (owners + estimated ETA):
- A1: Add a short-circuit to the priming heuristic to pre-warm top-N prefixes observed in last 24h across APAC (owner: Diego Ramos) — ETA: 2026-11-03.
- A2: Reduce sidecar metrics aggregation window from 15s -> 5s in edge agent to reduce autoscale oscillation (owner: Maya Chen) — ETA: 2026-11-10 (risk: increased metrics traffic to control plane).
- A3: Add a signature-level mismatch check in fallback routing that prefers compatible quantization family to avoid cold-model artifacts (owner: Omar Ibrahim) — ETA: 2026-11-17.
- A4: Draft a postmortem template snippet for "throttle-token-exhausted" class to be added to runbook (owner: Nora Patel) — ETA: 2026-11-05.

Signal recipe (quick reference) — local edge policy:
- queue_depth > 250 for > 30s -> lift token window to +20% if free reserved capacity exists; emit alert at SEV3.
- queue_depth > 400 -> begin 25% instant fallbacks to region_secondary (Tokyo), escalate to SEV2 if sustained > 2m.
- p99 latency > 500ms for short-gen -> reduce long-gen concurrency via request-weighted throttling.
- error_rate (throttle-token-exhausted) > 0.2% over 1m -> trigger immediate runbook step: increase reserved pool and notify ops.

Manual handoff notes (human ops):
- Midday run: ops lead (Asha) paged on first fallback wave at 11:53 SGT; we kept ops page open for entire window. Handoff checklist used: quick signal snapshot, current autoscale target, priming status, fallback fraction.
- Suggested refinement: create an ops "cueboard" view that collapses these four items into a single tile for quick triage. (Low-effort UI request).

Short-term mitigation we implemented during run:
- Temporary increase of reserved_capacity in ap-southeast1 by 15% (manual tweak via console) at 12:02 SGT, which reduced fallback fraction by ~9% during final wave.
- Triggered a manual priming wave for top-200 prefixes at 12:07 SGT which improved cache hit ratio by 7% after ~65s.

Follow-up experiments to schedule:
- Exp A: Synthetic mix variant that reuses prefixes more aggressively to validate priming heuristic vs synthetic diversity (owner: Diego) — schedule next week.
- Exp B: Canary a fallback-route model variant that uses same quantization family (tokyo-quant-compat) for a small traffic fraction; examine artifact rate (owner: Omar) — schedule after A2.
- Exp C: Run a metrics emitter stress test to validate 5s aggregation window feasibility (owner: Maya + infra perf) — schedule immediate.

Draft runbook excerpt (for runbook authors):
1) If throttles observed and queue_depth > 400: enable fallback ramp to region_secondary at 25% and notify ops.
2) If error class "throttle-token-exhausted" > 0.5%: increase reserved pool and open SEV2 bridge.
3) If priming lag persists > 90s: run top-prefix forced pre-warm and schedule a follow-up to optimize priming heuristics.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Do we need to expose a simple toggle to prefer "quantization-family-aware" fallback vs "lowest-latency" fallback for customers who prefer fidelity over latency?
- How many extra reserved units are cost-effective for each region during predictable local-business-hours surges? (cost model required).
- Are there edge scheduler changes required to avoid oversubscription of sidecar collectors?
